stories.title: Nalcorp, Clipper Equity Buy Coney Island Oceanfront Development Site for $20M
stories.excerpt: Fancy a trip to the Boardwalk? A pair of New York-based real estate development and investment firms — Nalcorp and Clipper Equity — have acquired a land parcel at 2015 Boardwalk West, an oceanfront development in Coney Island, Brooklyn, from seller Bath Site LLC for $20 million, broker TerraCRG announced Friday. The parking lot property, which spans 69,530 square feet and has 247 feet of Boardwalk frontage, seems to be part of a larger ongoing development on the site. Permits were filed in 2024 to build a 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building at 2015 Boardwalk West. The larger parcel of land home to the development was purchased in 2006 by the City Investment Fund — a real estate private equity vehicle launched by the Fisher Brothers and Morgan Stanley — from Thor Equities for $90 million. Following the 2006 sale, the larger parcel was subdivided into six separate tax lots, including the one part of this most recent transaction, which is called Block 7072, Lot 6. Bath Site LLC — an entity comprising Georgica Green Ventures and its nonprofit partner RiseBoro Community Partnership — acquired this property in July 2024 for $10.4 million. Dan Marks and Daniel Lebor from TerraCRG represented Bath Site LLC in this transaction. The firm did not disclose the names of the brokers who represented the buyers. The buyers did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment, while the seller could not be reached for comment. “Coney Island has become one of New York City’s most exciting waterfront growth stories,” Marks said in a statement. “Ongoing public and private investment has transformed the area into one of the city’s most compelling waterfront markets. As a result, opportunities to acquire premier development sites along the Boardwalk have become increasingly limited, making this one of the most significant development transactions in the neighborhood in recent years.” Nalcorp’s been busy in New York City, as it recently
bullets: Nalcorp & Clipper Equity acquire Coney Island parking lot for $20M; 247 ft Boardwalk frontage.
Site part of approved 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use development; permits filed 2024.
Larger parcel subdivided into six tax lots since City Investment Fund's 2006 $90M acquisition.
stories.summary: Nalcorp and Clipper Equity purchased a 69,530-square-foot oceanfront parking lot (Block 7072, Lot 6) in Coney Island for $20 million from Bath Site LLC. The parcel is part of a larger development site with approved permits for a 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building. The broader 6-lot site was acquired by City Investment Fund in 2006 for $90 million and has since been subdivided for phased development.
stories.impact: Coney Island's oceanfront mixed-use pipeline continues advancing despite financing headwinds. The segmented acquisition strategy suggests lower upfront capital per lot and risk-tiering; demand for Brooklyn oceanfront mixed-use remains strong enough to justify $20M+ land purchases ahead of uncertain capital markets. Watch for rental absorption rates once 202 units deliver—signals broader Brooklyn-Queens multifamily feasibility in 2026+.

stories.title: HGA, Mortenson Complete 620K-SF Surgical Center in Minneapolis
stories.excerpt: Interdisciplinary design firm HGA has completed the Richard M. Schulze Surgical and Critical Care Center, a 10-story, 620,000-square-foot addition to Abbott Northwestern Hospital housing 190 private inpatient rooms. The design firm worked with Allina Health to integrate new critical care spaces, including 30 advanced operating rooms purpose-built for complex procedures, into the campus’s existing facilities. The $1 billion, 10-story tower is part of a campus revitalization project at Abbott Northwestern Hospital. The team transformed the historic Founder’s Mall into a welcoming arrival garden and added a 27,000-square-foot rooftop garden offering panoramic views of the city. HGA is serving as the architect on the project, with Mortenson as the construction manager. “Our team worked closely with Allina Health to design a facility that expands access to specialized medical services today while remaining flexible enough to adapt to tomorrow’s technologies, clinical needs and healthcare delivery models,” said Jennifer Klund, Principal at HGA. The post HGA, Mortenson Complete 620K-SF Surgical Center in Minneapolis appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: HGA & Mortenson complete $1B, 10-story, 620K-SF surgical center addition at Abbott Northwestern Hospital, Minneapolis.
190 private inpatient rooms, 30 advanced operating rooms; part of broader campus revitalization.
Healthcare campus expansion signals institutional reinvestment; includes new public spaces and rooftop gardens.
stories.summary: HGA and Mortenson completed the Richard M. Schulze Surgical and Critical Care Center, a $1 billion, 10-story, 620,000-square-foot addition to Abbott Northwestern Hospital in Minneapolis. The facility houses 190 private inpatient rooms and 30 advanced operating rooms integrated with Allina Health's existing critical care infrastructure. The project included landscape and public realm improvements, positioning the campus as a major institutional anchor.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, a $1B healthcare capex project by a major metro anchor employer signals institutional confidence in Minneapolis real estate fundamentals and downtown/midtown vitality. Could support indirect demand for workforce housing near the hospital corridor, but unlikely to move multifamily underwriting. Low priority for TCR.

stories.title: Survey: 61% of Investors Hold Negative Multifamily Outlook in 2026, Per Berkadia
stories.excerpt: Housing isn’t making anyone happy these days. In a survey of more than 100 principals and executives across private real estate investment firms, Berkadia found that 61 percent of respondents characterized their outlook for the multifamily market in the second half of 2026 as negative, Commercial Observer can first report. Meanwhile, 52 percent said that the asset class performed worse in the first half of the year than they had anticipated. “Six months ago, investors were very optimistic that [volatility] was going to fade and transaction activity was going to accelerate,” said Josh Bodin, senior vice president of capital markets strategy and trading at Berkadia, in a conversation with CO. “Instead, the operating environment has remained a lot more uncertain, interest rate volatility has persisted and property performance has stayed softer than expected,” he added. Bond yields have been high for most of 2026. The 10-Year Treasury currently sits at 4.7 percent, its highest levels since 2023, while the 30-Year Treasury sits at 5.2 percent, a 20-year high. In a separate report, CBRE found that first-quarter investment sales in multifamily hit $29.5 billion, a 6 percent decline year-over-year, while the second quarter saw a rebound of investment sales activity to $34.9 billion (that total was still down by 2.7 percent year-over-year). However, Bodin emphasized these metrics and investors’ sentiments haven’t translated into a loss of confidence in multifamily as an asset class, but has instead changed how investors view execution risk. To this end, Berkadia’s survey found that 82 percent of investors plan to expand their portfolios in the coming months and that 83 percent expect market conditions to improve by late 2027. “On the tailwinds side, near-term, supply deliveries are beginning to moderate in many markets, capital remains really available for well-positioned assets and investors increasingly expect conditions to improve,” said Bodin. bullets: Berkadia survey: 61% of 100+ investment principals hold negative multifamily outlook for H2 2026.
52% report H1 2026 performance worse than expected; interest rate volatility, softer rents cited.
10-Year Treasury at 4.7%, 30-Year at 5.2% (20-year high); cap rates remain elevated.
stories.summary: A Berkadia survey of more than 100 real estate investment principals found 61% hold a negative multifamily outlook for the second half of 2026, with 52% reporting worse-than-expected H1 2026 performance. Respondents cited persistent interest rate volatility and softer operating fundamentals. The 10-Year Treasury stands at 4.7% and the 30-Year at 5.2% (a 20-year high), constraining financing availability and valuation multiples.
stories.impact: Widespread investor pessimism and elevated long-duration rates severely pressure multifamily development underwriting, particularly for speculative or value-add deals. Expect ongoing cap-rate pressure (likely 5.5%–6.5%+ depending on market/quality tier), higher leverage costs, and reduced buyer pools. Developers with pre-entitlement land or completed stabilized assets have advantage; new-starts will face slower absorption and margin compression. This is a 2026 headwind that may extend into 2027 if Treasury yields persist.

stories.title: St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort Secures $263M Refi After Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has rescued Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company (ARTIC)’s St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort out of special servicing, supplying a $263 million loan to refinance the oceanfront property. The New York-based lender assumed $188 million in existing debt and added $70 million in new debt backing the 213-room property in Bal Harbour, Fla., north of Miami Beach, according to public mortgage documents, which valued the asset at $311 million. The new financing comes nearly a year after a $188 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan tied to the resort headed to special servicing as the financing was set to mature. Although the loan remained current and the resort maintained a debt service coverage ratio above break-even, its cash flow in 2024 was about half of 2021 levels, the year it had secured the debt. The lender, Column Financial, wanted ARTIC to buy a replacement interest rate cap, which it had yet to secure, Morningstar reported. ARTIC, which is run by a member of the Qatari ruling family, had purchased the resort for $213 million in 2014, three years after it was completed. The complex, which features three 27-story towers at 9703 Collins Avenue, houses two pools, a 14,000-square-foot spa, five dining outposts, 13,000 square feet of event space as well as a condo component. The hotel owner and condo owners have sparred. In 2024, the condo association sued ARTIC over alleged building defects, safety hazards, and financial mismanagement. The parties settled the suit a year later. Fortress Investment Group and ARTIC did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Fortress rescues St. Regis Bal Harbour from special servicing with $263M refinance; valued at $311M.
Resort's 2024 cash flow ~50% of 2021 levels; assumed $188M existing debt, added $70M new debt.
Interest rate cap requirement triggered special servicing; hospitality asset stress visible despite oceanfront luxury positioning.
stories.summary: Fortress Investment Group refinanced the St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort (213 rooms) with a $263 million loan, rescuing it from special servicing. The new financing assumed $188 million in existing debt and added $70 million in new capital, with the asset valued at $311 million. The property's 2024 cash flow was approximately 50% of 2021 levels, and special servicing was triggered when the sponsor could not secure a replacement interest rate cap.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily impact, but signals distress in luxury hospitality—a bellwether for high-end real estate financing stress. The Bal Harbour resort's cash-flow collapse and refinance rescue demonstrate that even trophy oceanfront assets face headwinds when rates remain elevated and travel/tourism demand softens. South Florida's capital availability is tightening; developers seeking construction financing or mezzanine capital should expect even tighter terms and lower leverage multiples.

stories.title: First Pioneer Properties Buys Queens Retail Center for $24M
stories.excerpt: New York-based real estate management and development firm First Pioneer Properties, along with ABS Partners Real Estate, has acquired a Queens retail center from Levy Properties for $23.5 million, property records made public Thursday show. The one-story property at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside is currently home to an urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store. Jennifer Markowitz of Levy Properties signed the deal for the seller, while Suresh Sani, owner of First Pioneer Properties, signed for the buyers. ABS seems to act as a frequent co-investor and partner of First Pioneer Properties. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. The buyers and seller did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. The property has 24,000 square feet of built space and 74,350 square feet of additional air rights for a total of 98,478 buildable square feet, according to data from PincusCo. The buyers’ intentions for the property are unclear, but Queens has been awash with multifamily developments lately. This month, Wells Fargo provided a $175 million construction loan to the Domain Companies for a 429-unit mixed-income housing development at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st Street in Astoria. Also this month, LMXD and BedRock Real Estate Partners closed on a $250 million loan to build a housing development at 35-10 Steinway Street in Astoria. Earlier this summer, another Queens retail property changed hands when Punia & Marx Real Estate sold the Whitestone Shopping Center at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway for $56 million. Meanwhile, a historic Queens bowling alley — Whitestone Lanes — at 30-05 Whitestone Expressway in Flushing — sold for $45 million in June as part of a major multifamily development project coming to the area. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: First Pioneer Properties & ABS Partners buy Bayside, Queens retail center for $23.5M from Levy Properties.
213-04 Northern Boulevard: 24K SF built, 74,350 SF air rights; currently urgent care & retail tenants.
Queens multifamily pipeline active; buyers' redevelopment intentions unclear but air rights suggest mixed-use upside.
stories.summary: First Pioneer Properties and ABS Partners acquired a retail center at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside, Queens for $23.5 million from Levy Properties. The one-story property totals 24,000 square feet of built space plus 74,350 square feet of air rights, currently occupied by an urgent care facility and retail tenant. Buyer intentions are unstated, but the substantial air rights signal potential mixed-use or residential redevelopment.
stories.impact: Queens air-rights retail acquisitions increasingly point to neighborhood densification and multifamily conversion/redevelopment potential. Bayside's market fundamentals (proximity to transit, median rents, underbuilt density) make this a candidate for mid-rise mixed-use redevelopment. The $23.5M entry price on ~98K buildable SF suggests ~$240/SF—reasonable for a low-intensity redevelopment play. Monitor Queens entitlements and construction financing—strong signal of near-term development pipeline in this submarket.

stories.title: Pinnacle Group Offloads $128M Condominium and Commercial Portfolio in NYC
stories.excerpt: Pinnacle Group has offloaded a $128 million residential and retail condominium portfolio in New York City, less than a year after selling off its rent-stabilized assets. The massive trade, filed in city records this week, spanned 39 transactions across Queens, Brooklyn and Manhattan. It included nearly 750 residential units, as well as dozens of retail condominiums and several parking lots. The Real Deal first reported on the sale. The buyer entities, Friar Park JW, share an address with law firm Kurzman Eisenberg Corbin & Lever. The transactions were signed by Stuart Berg, chair of the firm’s real estate practice group. A PincusCo report tied the Friar Park entities and Berg to Tremada Holdings, an affiliate of London-based property company William Pears Group. The group, through Tremada, has quietly executed bulk residential transactions across New York City over the years with Berg’s law firm, according to PincusCo. Berg, as well as spokespeople for William Pears Group and Tremada, did not respond to requests for comment. Queens-based property management company Bronstein Properties is the managing agent for the portfolio of units, according to a spokesperson for Bronstein. Pinnacle, led by Joel Wiener, made headlines in May 2025 when it placed a portfolio of roughly 5,000 rent-stabilized apartments across New York City into bankruptcy after facing approximately $574.4 million in debt. Summit Properties won the auction for the portfolio in January, paying $451.3 million for the units. The proceeds from Pinnacle’s most recent sale will pay $66 million to lender Axos Capital, TRD reported, citing filings with the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange by Pinnacle’s Israeli subsidiary Zarasai Group. Another $47 million is currently slated to be deposited into the account of Series C bondholders. A spokesperson for Pinnacle Group could not be reached for comment on the sales. bullets: Pinnacle Group offloads $128M NYC condominium & retail portfolio: 39 transactions, ~750 units across Queens, Brooklyn, Manhattan.
Buyer entities (Friar Park JW) linked to Tremada Holdings (William Pears Group, London-based); bulk residential play.
Pinnacle exits after divesting rent-stabilized assets; signals portfolio reconfiguration amid financing headwinds.
stories.summary: Pinnacle Group sold a $128 million residential and retail condominium portfolio spanning 39 transactions and approximately 750 units across Queens, Brooklyn, and Manhattan. The buyer entities, Friar Park JW, are tied to Tremada Holdings, an affiliate of London-based William Pears Group, which has been executing bulk residential transactions in NYC through associated legal counsel. The sale follows Pinnacle's earlier divestiture of rent-stabilized assets.
stories.impact: International capital (William Pears Group/Tremada) quietly acquiring NYC residential bulk portfolios signals confidence in long-hold value despite near-term financing stress. The shift from rent-stabilized (Pinnacle) to mixed-tenure condo portfolios reflects different risk-return profiles and financing flexibility. This is a strategic repositioning play—bulk buys lock in low basis, hedge currency/market timing risk, and position for slower exit cycles. For TCR: Watch for similar bulk dispositions from over-leveraged sponsors; opportunity for selective acquisitions at compressed valuations if financing is solved.

stories.title: Office, Industrial Occupancy Rates Edge Up in The Woodlands
stories.excerpt: Vacancy rates in The Woodlands area grew slightly in retail and industrial sectors in August, while the office sector saw a slight decrease when compared to the third quarter of 2025, according to commercial real estate data from Caldwell Cos. Community Impact reports that rental rates per square foot for retail units grew between the third quarter of 2025 and early August, by $3.70 per square foot. Office units in the Woodlands area saw a $1.96 per square foot increase in monthly leasing rates in the same period. Industrial units follow the same trend of slow increases since the third quarter of 2023. New construction for the industrial sector has slowed in both new buildings and square footage since the third quarter of 2025, with 14 buildings underway as of Aug. 4 compared to 30 about a year ago. Retail sector construction is down slightly in the same time period. The post Office, Industrial Occupancy Rates Edge Up in The Woodlands appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: The Woodlands, TX: office, retail, industrial occupancy slightly up; retail rents +$3.70/SF, office +$1.96/SF YoY.
Industrial construction slowed: 14 buildings underway (Aug 2026) vs. 30 a year prior; new supply moderation.
Retail & industrial new construction down slightly; slowdown correlates with broader Texas market cooling.
stories.summary: The Woodlands, Texas saw modest occupancy improvements across retail and industrial in early August 2026, with rental rate increases: retail up $3.70/SF and office up $1.96/SF since Q3 2025. However, new industrial construction slowed significantly, with only 14 buildings underway as of early August compared to 30 a year prior. Retail construction also declined slightly.
stories.impact: Industrial new-supply moderation in The Woodlands (Houston's largest master-planned community) mirrors broader Texas market cooling and suggests developer caution due to elevated cap rates and financing costs. Slowing starts may reduce immediate supply pressure but signal soft demand expectations. For multifamily: The Woodlands is a high-income, family-oriented submarket; slower industrial/commercial growth could soften employment-driven apartment demand. Monitor Houston-area multifamily absorption; if The Woodlands stalls, rents may remain under pressure despite existing shortage.

stories.title: Varia US, Brookfield Launch $694M Multifamily Joint Venture
stories.excerpt: Varia US Properties AG, the Swiss-listed investor in the U.S. multifamily sector, externally managed by Stoneweg, an SWI Group Company, has formed a US$693.9 million two-vehicle joint venture with affiliates of Brookfield Asset Management for 13 of Varia’s 17-property U.S. multifamily portfolio. The JV provides access to up to US$200 million equity capital to fund future acquisitions, enabling Varia US to expand its portfolio and reposition the Company towards a higher-quality portfolio. Varia US will actively invest in the JV assets to maximize value ahead of planned disposals. Comprising 4,112 units across nine U.S. states, the 13 properties have been divided into two newly formed vehicles, with an aggregate gross asset value of approximately $694 million. Four properties will remain wholly owned and consolidated by Varia US. Max-Herve George, co-founder and CEO of SWI Group, said, “This joint venture gives us the firepower and the flexibility to concentrate on high-quality residential communities, while positioning Varia US to grow decisively as the U.S. living sector continues to reward scale and discipline.” Pictured: Varia US’ Rolling Hills Apartments in Louisville, KY. Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Gain firsthand insights from industry leaders on capital markets, development, operations, financing, and investment trends while expanding your network with the people making deals happen. See you on September 22! The post Varia US, Brookfield Launch $694M Multifamily Joint Venture appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Varia US & Brookfield launch $694M JV; 13 of Varia's 17 U.S. properties (4,112 units, 9 states).
JV provides access to $200M equity capital for future acquisitions; Varia retains 4 properties wholly.
Strategy: reposition toward higher-quality assets; active value-add and disposals planned.
stories.summary: Varia US Properties AG (Swiss-listed, externally managed by Stoneweg) formed a $694 million joint venture with Brookfield Asset Management affiliates covering 13 of its 17 U.S. multifamily properties (4,112 units across 9 states). The JV provides access to $200 million in equity capital to fund future acquisitions and supports repositioning toward higher-quality assets. Varia retains 4 properties wholly owned.
stories.impact: Mid-sized multifamily owner pairs with mega-capital (Brookfield) to unlock $200M growth capital despite unfavorable financing environment. This JV structure reflects capital scarcity: smaller sponsors trade equity/control for access to dry powder and institutional LP backing. The $200M equity cushion and planned disposals signal active portfolio optimization in a down market—sell C/D assets, upgrade to A/B with leverage. For TCR: Brookfield's $694M commitment validates U.S. multifamily as an inflation-hedged asset class even amid near-term headwinds; expect Brookfield to be an active acquirer of stabilized, core-plus assets in 2026–2027, creating competition for capital and pricing pressure.

stories.title: Logistics Plus Signs 744K-SF Wilmer Warehouse Lease
stories.excerpt: Logistics Plus has signed a 744,452-square-foot industrial lease in the southern Dallas suburb of Wilmer. The Pennsylvania-based provider of freight and fulfillment services will occupy the entire Building 2 within the Southport Logistics Center, an approximately 1.5 million-square-foot development. Building 2 features 123 dock doors, three drive-in doors and 4,647 square feet of speculative office space. Building 1, still vacant, includes 121 dock doors, four drive-in doors, 389 car parking spaces, 170 trailer parking spaces, and 3,534 square feet of speculative office space. Kurt Griffin and Nathan Orbin of JLL represented the landlord, a joint venture between Bandera Ventures and Invesco Real Estate, in the lease negotiations. In addition to the Wilmer site, Logistics Plus has another warehouse in Haslet. The facilities have a combined 2 million square feet of storage space in the region. Logistics Plus has over 12 million square feet of commercial warehouse space across North America. The post Logistics Plus Signs 744K-SF Wilmer Warehouse Lease appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Logistics Plus leases entire 744K-SF Building 2 at Southport Logistics Center, Wilmer, Dallas suburb.
JV landlord (Bandera Ventures & Invesco Real Estate); 123 dock doors, 4,647 SF office space.
Logistics demand steady; no multifamily relevance but signals industrial leasing activity in Dallas metro.
stories.summary: Logistics Plus, a Pennsylvania-based freight and fulfillment provider, signed a full-building lease for 744,452 square feet (Building 2) at the Southport Logistics Center in Wilmer, a southern Dallas suburb. The facility features 123 dock doors and 4,647 square feet of speculative office. The landlord is a joint venture of Bandera Ventures and Invesco Real Estate. Logistics Plus operates over 12 million square feet of warehouse space across North America.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. Strong industrial leasing demand in Dallas' southern suburbs supports continued logistics-driven job growth and potential indirect apartments demand nearby (workforce housing). However, industrial tenancy doesn't directly drive multifamily development feasibility or capital. Monitor Dallas metro job growth and rent trends; sustained industrial leasing may support broader demographic inflow and apartment demand, but this deal alone is insufficient signal.
